description: First 50 seeds only - testing 'starting well' quality

phrases.english: you wanted to speak with me
phrases.other: tu voulais parler avec moi
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French is correct and idiomatic.

phrases.english: I wasn't thinking here
phrases.other: je ne pensais pas ici
phrases.notes: English is awkward - 'I wasn't thinking here' is semantically odd. French is grammatically correct but doesn't make sense as a phrase anyone would say.

phrases.english: I'm not sure what's going to happen after you finish
phrases.other: je ne suis pas sur de ce qui va se passer apres que tu termines
phrases.notes: English is natural. French is grammatically correct - 'apres que' technically takes indicative in modern French. Could use subjunctive but indicative is acceptable.

phrases.english: I was starting to feel okay
phrases.other: je commencais a me sentir bien
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French correctly uses imperfect for ongoing state and reflexive 'se sentir'.

phrases.english: as hard as possible
phrases.other: aussi dur que possible
phrases.notes: Both natural and correct. Fragment but usable. 'Aussi fort que possible' could also work depending on context.

phrases.english: or if I need to improve very well this morning
phrases.other: ou si je dois m'ameliorer tres bien ce matin
phrases.notes: English is nonsensical - 'improve very well' is not grammatical. You improve something, not 'improve very well'. French follows the same nonsense.

phrases.english: I started to learn this morning
phrases.other: j'ai commence a apprendre ce matin
phrases.notes: Natural and correct in both languages. Good use of passe compose for completed action.

phrases.english: are you learning quickly
phrases.other: apprends-tu rapidement
phrases.notes: English natural. French uses formal inversion which is correct but slightly formal. 'Tu apprends vite?' would be more casual.

phrases.english: I'm a little ready to go now
phrases.other: je suis un peu pret a partir maintenant
phrases.notes: English is awkward - 'a little ready' is unusual. You're either ready or not. French mirrors this awkwardness. 'Almost ready' would be natural.

phrases.english: we want to meet quickly this evening
phrases.other: nous voulons nous retrouver rapidement ce soir
phrases.notes: English is slightly awkward - 'meet quickly' is unusual. French is grammatically correct. 'Meet briefly' would be more natural.

phrases.english: I wouldn't like to explain what I mean to someone else
phrases.other: je n'aimerais pas expliquer ce que je veux dire a quelqu'un d'autre
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French correctly uses conditional and the expression 'ce que je veux dire'.

phrases.english: I feel okay but I'm starting to feel tired
phrases.other: je me sens bien mais je commence a me sentir fatigue
phrases.notes: Natural and correct in both languages. Good use of reflexive 'se sentir'.

phrases.english: I started to learn the story
phrases.other: j'ai commence a apprendre l'histoire
phrases.notes: English is slightly odd - 'learn the story' is borderline. You learn a story, but 'read' or 'hear' might be more natural. French is correct.

phrases.english: what's going to happen
phrases.other: ce qui va se passer
phrases.notes: Perfect and natural in both languages. Excellent use of 'ce qui' with reflexive.

phrases.english: I can explain what I mean
phrases.other: je peux expliquer ce que je veux dire
phrases.notes: Perfect and natural in both languages. 'Ce que je veux dire' is idiomatic French.

phrases.english: I'm not sure if I can
phrases.other: je ne suis pas sur si je peux
phrases.notes: English is natural. French 'sur si' is slightly awkward - 'je ne sais pas si je peux' or 'je ne suis pas sur de pouvoir' would be more idiomatic.

phrases.english: I'm going to practise now
phrases.other: je vais m'entrainer maintenant
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French correctly uses reflexive 's'entrainer' with near future.

phrases.english: if you know what I think
phrases.other: si tu vois ce que je pense
phrases.notes: English 'if you know what I think' is not a common phrase. 'If you know what I mean' is standard. French uses 'vois' (see) which creates a mismatch with 'know'.

phrases.english: I wanted to ask you to speak French
phrases.other: je voulais te demander de parler francais
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. Good use of imperfect for polite request and 'demander de'.

phrases.english: I want to speak French when other people are here
phrases.other: je veux parler francais quand d'autres personnes sont ici
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French is grammatically correct.

phrases.english: after tomorrow
phrases.other: apres demain
phrases.notes: English is functional. French 'apres-demain' should be hyphenated as it's a compound word meaning 'the day after tomorrow'. Without hyphen it could mean 'after tomorrow' literally.

phrases.english: before this evening
phrases.other: avant ce soir
phrases.notes: Natural and correct in both languages.

phrases.english: because this evening
phrases.other: parce que ce soir
phrases.notes: Both are fragments that need completion. Grammatically correct but incomplete thoughts.

phrases.english: are you going to help me learn French soon
phrases.other: vas-tu m'aider a apprendre le francais bientot
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French inversion is formal but correct.

phrases.english: she doesn't like taking too much time to answer later on
phrases.other: elle n'aime pas prendre trop de temps pour repondre plus tard
phrases.notes: Both languages natural. French correct. Slightly complex but valid.

phrases.english: we don't want to read
phrases.other: nous ne voulons pas lire
phrases.notes: Natural and correct in both languages. Uses 'nous' form which is correct.

phrases.english: I can try to explain something to someone else in French today
phrases.other: je peux essayer d'expliquer quelque chose a quelqu'un d'autre en francais aujourd'hui
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French is grammatically correct with proper use of 'd'expliquer' contraction.

phrases.english: or if I need to improve today
phrases.other: ou si je dois m'ameliorer aujourd'hui
phrases.notes: English 'improve' needs an object or context - improve at what? French uses reflexive correctly but inherits the vagueness.

phrases.english: we don't want to be quiet
phrases.other: nous ne voulons pas etre silencieux
phrases.notes: Natural in both. French uses 'silencieux' which is correct. Could also be 'nous ne voulons pas nous taire' for emphasis.

phrases.english: we don't want to interrupt
phrases.other: nous ne voulons pas interrompre
phrases.notes: Natural and correct in both languages.

phrases.english: I wanted to start speaking French with everyone else this evening
phrases.other: je voulais commencer a parler francais avec tout le monde ce soir
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French is correct with good use of 'tout le monde'.

phrases.english: I wouldn't like to guess what you mean today
phrases.other: je n'aimerais pas deviner ce que tu veux dire aujourd'hui
phrases.notes: Both natural. French correctly uses conditional and 'ce que tu veux dire'.

phrases.english: she doesn't want to go
phrases.other: elle ne veut pas partir
phrases.notes: Perfect and natural in both languages.

phrases.english: how long to answer
phrases.other: depuis combien de temps pour repondre
phrases.notes: English is ungrammatical/incomplete - needs context like 'how long to answer?' as question or 'how long to wait before answering'. French translation doesn't match - 'depuis combien de temps' means 'for how long (since)' which implies duration from past, not 'how long to'.

phrases.english: she doesn't want to think about it this afternoon
phrases.other: elle ne veut pas y reflechir cet apres-midi
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. Good use of 'y' for 'about it' and 'reflechir' for deeper thinking.

phrases.english: read the story this afternoon
phrases.other: lire l'histoire cet apres-midi
phrases.notes: English imperative is natural. French infinitive form is correct for instructions/titles. Uses correct 'cet' before vowel.

phrases.english: I'm not sure if I want to try to explain what I mean today
phrases.other: je ne suis pas sur si je veux essayer d'expliquer ce que je veux dire aujourd'hui
phrases.notes: Both natural but French 'sur si' is slightly awkward as noted before. Long but grammatically correct.

phrases.english: he wants to speak French with someone else all day tomorrow
phrases.other: il veut parler francais avec quelqu'un d'autre toute la journee demain
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French uses 'toute la journee' correctly with feminine agreement.

phrases.english: are you going to help me learn to speak French before this evening
phrases.other: vas-tu m'aider a apprendre a parler francais avant ce soir
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. Good structure with double infinitive construction.

phrases.english: he wants to encounter people who speak French soon
phrases.other: il veut rencontrer des gens qui parlent francais bientot
phrases.notes: English 'encounter' is formal/literary - 'meet' would be more natural. French 'rencontrer' is perfect and natural.

phrases.english: she wants to help me before I have to go soon
phrases.other: elle veut m'aider avant que je doive partir bientot
phrases.notes: English natural. French correctly uses subjunctive 'doive' after 'avant que'. Slightly awkward placing of 'bientot'.

phrases.english: you speak French very well
phrases.other: tu parles francais tres bien
phrases.notes: Natural in both. French word order 'tres bien' at end is correct. 'Tu parles tres bien francais' also acceptable.

phrases.english: I wasn't thinking about it this morning after learning all day
phrases.other: je ne pensais pas a y ce matin apres apprendre toute la journee
phrases.notes: English is odd - 'after learning all day' doesn't fit with 'this morning'. French has grammatical error: 'a y' is wrong (should be just 'y' or 'a ca'), and 'apres apprendre' should be 'apres avoir appris'.

phrases.english: I am looking forward to speaking French this afternoon
phrases.other: j'ai hate de parler francais cet apres-midi
phrases.notes: Excellent in both languages. 'J'ai hate de' is the idiomatic way to express 'looking forward to'.

phrases.english: I like feeling as if
phrases.other: j'aime me sentir comme si
phrases.notes: Both are incomplete fragments. 'As if' needs a following clause. French mirrors this incompleteness.

phrases.english: help me learn before this evening
phrases.other: m'aider a apprendre avant ce soir
phrases.notes: English imperative is natural. French infinitive construction is correct for requests.

phrases.english: I want to try to speak French with you
phrases.other: je veux essayer de parler francais avec toi
phrases.notes: Perfect and natural in both languages. Good use of 'essayer de'.

phrases.english: to speak after you finish
phrases.other: parler apres que tu termines
phrases.notes: Both are fragments but usable. French uses indicative after 'apres que' which is correct in modern usage.

phrases.english: did you want to speak with me tonight
phrases.other: tu voulais parler avec moi ce soir
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French uses imperfect for polite past question.

phrases.english: I am not going to learn
phrases.other: je ne vais pas apprendre
phrases.notes: Natural in both languages. French correctly uses near future negative.

worst_3_phrases.english: or if I need to improve very well this morning
worst_3_phrases.other: ou si je dois m'ameliorer tres bien ce matin
worst_3_phrases.reason: The English phrase 'improve very well' is fundamentally ungrammatical. You can 'improve greatly' or 'do very well' but not 'improve very well'. The French mirrors this nonsense. This appears to be a failed LEGO combination.

worst_3_phrases.other: depuis combien de temps pour repondre
worst_3_phrases.reason: English is an incomplete, ungrammatical fragment. The French translation uses 'depuis combien de temps' which means 'for how long (since when)' - a duration from the past - which doesn't match the English intent. Should be something like 'combien de temps pour repondre' if asking about time needed.

worst_3_phrases.english: I wasn't thinking about it this morning after learning all day
worst_3_phrases.other: je ne pensais pas a y ce matin apres apprendre toute la journee
worst_3_phrases.reason: Multiple issues: (1) English has logical inconsistency - 'this morning' vs 'after learning all day'; (2) French 'a y' is grammatically wrong - should be just 'y' as 'penser a' + 'y' = 'y penser'; (3) 'apres apprendre' is wrong - should be 'apres avoir appris' (after having learned).

strengths: Good use of French contractions and reflexive verbs
Proper use of tenses (imperfect, passe compose, conditional)
weaknesses: Some English source phrases are unnatural or ungrammatical
A few LEGO combinations produce nonsensical output
Some incomplete fragments that lack context
Occasional 'sur si' construction in French (slightly awkward)
recommendations: Review source phrases idx 6, 34, 43 - these need regeneration
Consider adding completion requirements for 'as if' phrases
Validate semantic coherence, not just grammatical correctness
Check that 'apres + infinitive' constructions use 'apres avoir/etre + past participle'
